inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 Annual Report note 31 share-based payments expense $49.9m (CPU.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:4993). Awards are settled by on-market purchases ($75.0m FY26, $34.0m FY25; cash flow statement :3167), which is the cash funding of the flat count, not an additional charge.
inputs.buyback_note: No formal buy-back in FY26 ($279.3m in FY25). $75.0m of on-market purchases for share-based awards kept the count flat; buy-back capacity is constrained by Australian tax law and management has shifted to dividends (FY26 DPS A$1.20, +29%).
inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted average diluted shares FY2026 579,737,415 (CPU.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:3423); 578.4m on issue at 30 June 2026. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows are USD (annual report: 'presented in United States dollars', :3183); ASX quote is AUD. AUD/USD 0.7113 (Yahoo AUDUSD=X, 2026-09-22T09:28Z), so fx_rate USD->AUD = 1/0.7113 = 1.4059. Parity check: A$41.69 x 0.7113 = US$29.65 vs CMSQF (OTC ordinary line) US$29.75 at the 2026-09-21 US close, a 0.3% tie confirming rate, direction and quote basis. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate; re-derive the rate on any refresh.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in USD, the flows' currency: risk-free 4.96% (US 10y, ^TNX 2026-09-21), ERP 5.0%, beta 0.85 (low-beta fiduciary processor, MI gives partial counter-cyclicality to rate cuts) -> cost of equity 9.2%; after-tax cost of debt ~4.5% at ~1% debt weight (net debt/EBITDA 0.11x) -> WACC 9.25%, rounded. One WACC across all three scenarios: the rate-cycle, capital-markets and margin risks are priced in the bear flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B): leases as operating cost. FY26 lease principal $24.8m (financing, :3173) plus interest on lease liabilities $7.8m (:4624) = $32.6m, 1.0% of revenue, charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path. Lease liabilities ($29.2m current + $128.8m non-current = $158.0m) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt; total_debt is borrowings only ($1,197.8m), matching the parser's core_metrics definition. D&A for the tax line is ex right-of-use depreciation: $174.4m total less $29.3m ROU = $145.1m (4.45% of revenue).
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI equity $2.6m and NCI profit $0.5m are immaterial (<0.1% of NPAT). Flows are whole-group; the $2.6m NCI stock is deducted once in the equity bridge.
inputs.ebitda_basis: ebitda_margin_path is PRE-SBC and on the STATUTORY basis, not Management EBITDA. FY26 statutory EBITDA $1,105.4m (33.9%) is after $49.9m SBC and includes a one-off $46.3m loss on the UK Mortgage Services sale (:1320); adding both back gives $1,201.6m / 36.9%. Management adjusted EBITDA of $1,284.9m (39.4%) also adds back ~$130m of recurring restructuring, cost-out and acquisition costs that have recurred every year since FY19 ($174-296m/yr); those are treated as real costs here. Anchor FY26 pre-SBC, ex-disposal-loss margin: ~36.5-36.9%.
inputs.margin_income_treatment: Margin income (interest on ~$31.7bn of average client balances, FY26 $748.7m = 23% of revenue at ~100% incremental margin) is OPERATING revenue, not interest on CPU's own cash, and stays inside revenue/EBITDA. FY27 guidance: MI ~$770m on $32.8bn balances at 2.35% yield, assuming one US hike (Jan), one Canada hike (Mar), two UK hikes (Nov, Mar) and hedged exposed balances rising from ~50% to ~60%. Sensitivity: roughly $8bn of unhedged exposed balances, so 100bp of unassumed cuts is ~-$80m EBITDA (~-2.5pp margin). Base holds MI at guidance then grows with balances; bear removes ~150bp of yield over FY27-28; bull adds ~50bp plus balance growth.
inputs.capex_note: FY26 payments for PP&E $35.4m (1.1% of revenue). The FY22-24 capex of $108-119m included mortgage servicing rights purchased by the divested US Mortgage Services business (sold 1 May 2024); continuing-operations capex is $35-44m. FY27 call colour flagged a step-up (~A$65m for facilities and AI), so capex is modelled at 1.8% of revenue in FY27 tapering to 1.5%. Software development is capitalised where it qualifies but has no separate cash-flow line.
inputs.interest_income_note: Set to 0: Computershare is net debt ($144.1m) so the section 1(b) strip does not apply. The $37.6m interest and dividends received (:3150) relates to gross cash of $1,053.7m that is netted against borrowings in the bridge; the engine's flows are unlevered so neither interest received nor the $93.7m interest paid is in the projections.
inputs.last_fcf_note: Owner FCF FY26 = reported FCF 801.2 (OCF 836.6 - PP&E capex 35.4) - SBC 49.9 - lease principal 24.8 (treatment B; the $7.8m lease interest is already inside OCF) - interest income 0 = 726.5. This levered figure is the record anchor only; the projections are built unlevered from EBITDA components and sit ~$45-90m higher in year 1 because after-tax net interest (~$43m) is no longer deducted.
inputs.cash_tax_note: FY26 cash taxes paid $202.1m on PBT $848.4m = 23.8%; income tax expense $229.2m = 27.0% ETR. Unlevered EBIT (pre-SBC EBITDA 1,155 - SBC 50 - lease 33 - D&A ex-ROU 145 = ~$927m) at 24% = $222m, above actual cash tax, so no shelter is being perpetuated. Ramped to 26% (blended US 21%+state, UK 25%, Australia 30%, Canada 26.5%) by year 5.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 2, operating company, non-US filer) with section 7 adaptations for currency (USD flows / AUD quote), IFRS-16 leases (treatment B) and NCI. Not a bank: the client balances that earn margin income are held in a fiduciary/custodial capacity and are not deposits on Computershare's balance sheet, so residual-income does not apply; not a REIT/LIC/holdco. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY.md entry). D&A/EBITDA continuity: FY24-FY26 bases are continuing-operations only (D&A 162-174 vs 280 whole-group FY23); the FY23 whole-group figures are not blended into any driver. Horizon 10 years: margins are near-mature but the D&A taper (acquired-intangible amortisation rolling off) and cash-tax ramp need the longer build. Working-capital capture 0%: receivables-led fee business, FY26 WC inflow treated as non-recurring.

equity_bridge.note: FY26 balance sheet :3062; whole-group flows, NCI stock deducted once

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance_anchored: FY27 headline revenue growth ~3.5% (5-7% underlying ex FY26 disposals), MI +2.8% to ~$770m, EBIT ex MI +3.5% (+7% underlying)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (0.1% 5yr, 2.2% 3yr) diverges >30% from revenue (7.4%) and EPS (25.9%) because Computershare pays out 60-75% of earnings, bought back $490m in FY24-25 and booked disposal losses; book value is not the growth anchor for this business. Revenue 3yr CAGR of 0.6% is depressed because FY23 is whole-group (incl. US Mortgage Services, sold May 2024) while FY26 is continuing operations; underlying continuing growth is 4-6%.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs use the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; interest income immaterial pre-FY23 and not stripped given net debt throughout; lease principal not deducted in the history because it is not in the CSV). Owner-FCF CAGR (18.3% 3yr) sits just above reported (17.9%) because SBC grew slower than cash flow. Both 5yr CAGRs start from the FY21 rate-trough (MI collapsed under zero rates) and overstate sustainable growth. Owner FCF: FY21 128.3, FY23 453.5, FY26 751.3 (ex lease).

base.growth_note: FY27 3.5% headline (disposal drag, event fees down, MI +2.8%); FY28 4.5% once the UK MS/CCS Germany drag lapses; fades to 2.5% by year 9 as fee growth converges on nominal GDP plus modest balance growth.
base.margin_note: FY26 pre-SBC statutory ex-disposal-loss ~36.9%; FY27 36.5% keeps a ~40bp cushion for stranded costs and recurring restructuring charges while EBIT ex MI margin reaches the guided ~19% and MI adds $21m; plateaus at 37.0% - cost-out ($22m) offset by wage/vendor inflation and technology reinvestment.
base.da_note: Ex-ROU D&A 4.45% of revenue in FY26 is inflated by amortisation of acquired intangibles (Wells Fargo CT, KCC); it tapers to 3.0% as those roll off, which reduces the tax shield - conservative in the right direction.
base.narrative: Steady compounder. Fee growth across all three segments, margin income held at guidance and growing with balances, cost-out and moderating inflation take pre-SBC EBITDA margin to 37%.

bull.narrative: Rates stay higher for longer and hedging locks in ~2.5-2.7% yields on growing balances (MI $820-850m by FY29); Corporate Trust structured-issuance and Employee Share Plans compound at high single digits; bolt-on M&A in Corporate Trust/Entity Solutions funded from 0.1x leverage adds 1-2pp of growth; stranded costs fully absorbed and management-adjustment charges shrink, lifting pre-SBC margin to 38.5%.

bear.narrative: The guided FY27 hikes do not happen and central banks cut ~150bp over FY27-28: MI falls ~$120-150m (half of exposed balances unhedged) at ~100% margin, taking ~4pp off EBITDA margin with only partial cost-out offset; a capital-markets slowdown cuts corporate-action, IPO and plan-transaction fees; Issuer Services margin pressure from the large-client repricing persists. Growth stalls in FY27-28 and recovers only to 2% nominal; terminal multiple capped at 15x.

scenario_narratives.base: Computershare delivers roughly its FY27 guidance: Management EPS ~154c (+6%), MI ~$770m on $32.8bn balances at 2.35%, EBIT ex MI margin ~19%, and thereafter compounds fee revenue at 3-4% with MI growing with balances. Pre-SBC statutory EBITDA margin settles at 37% (Management EBITDA less ~$130m/yr of recurring restructuring/acquisition costs treated as real). Capex normalises to 1.5-1.8% of revenue after the FY27 AI/facilities step-up. No M&A is assumed; the 0.1x-levered balance sheet is optionality, not value.
scenario_narratives.bull: MI proves to have bottomed and rates stay elevated: hedged yields lock in 2.5%+ on balances growing to $35bn+, Corporate Trust keeps taking share in structured products, Employee Share Plans compounds at high single digits on rising assets under administration, and disciplined bolt-ons add growth. Margin expands to 38.5% pre-SBC as stranded costs and management-adjustment charges fade. Terminal growth 3%, cap 20x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The rate-cycle axis breaks against the company: no FY27 hikes and ~150bp of cuts across USD/GBP/CAD compress MI by $120-150m, which drops nearly straight to EBIT. A weaker equity/M&A cycle removes event fees and plan-transaction revenue at the same time, and the Issuer Services margin compression seen in FY26 (-300bp) proves structural. Revenue stalls for two years and margins reset to 32.5-33%; the market re-rates the stock to a 15x FCF exit.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25% because the single largest earnings swing factor - the central-bank rate path behind ~23% of revenue at ~100% margin - is entirely outside management's control, and FY27 guidance explicitly depends on four rate hikes across three currencies that markets do not treat as certain. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it requires three independent things to go right: MI recovery, core-margin expansion despite the FY26 Issuer Services compression, and accretive M&A. Base at 50%: a 48-year-old oligopoly registrar with 57% of the S&P 500 and very low churn is a genuinely predictable fee business outside the rate overlay.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Computershare is a high-quality, capital-light fiduciary processor whose fee base is annuity-like, but roughly a quarter of revenue and a larger share of profit is a rate bet the company does not control. The house DCF values the fee business plus margin income at guidance, charges recurring 'management adjustments' as real costs, expenses SBC and lease cost once, discounts USD flows at a USD-built 9.25% WACC, and converts to AUD at a parity-checked rate. The market is paying ~21x unlevered owner FCF, which at this WACC implies either a lower discount rate or perpetual growth above 4%; the gap between the weighted IV and the price is the premium being paid for predictability and the MI-recovery narrative.
key_risks_to_valuation: Rate path: 100bp of unassumed cuts on ~$8bn of unhedged exposed balances is ~-$80m EBITDA (~-2.5pp margin), the bear-case axis
Recurring management adjustments ($130-300m/yr since FY19) are treated as costs here; a reader using Management EBITDA will get a ~15% higher value
Capital-markets cyclicality in event fees, corporate actions and plan transactions - FY26 had non-repeating HK IPO and event-fee tailwinds
Issuer Services margin compression (-300bp FY26) tied to a large client contract may be structural rather than one-off
FX: value is built in USD and converted at AUD/USD 0.7113; a 5% AUD move changes the AUD IV by 5% with no change in the business
Terminal value is ~55% of EV; the exit multiple implied by Gordon at 9.25%/2.5% is ~15x FCF against the ~21x the market pays today
